key_insight: Newsroom AI can influence more than what information is shown—it can also shape how a story feels, which affects whether people trust, approach, and share it. The paper argues that these emotional effects must be tested with behavioural evaluation, not just accuracy metrics.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of evaluating AI systems that optimize emotional packaging in journalism. It asks how to ensure that emotionally tuned content still helps accurate information reach readers without unintentionally distorting trust or engagement.
method: Proposes behavioural evaluation of newsroom AI rather than relying only on technical performance measures.
Focuses on testing how emotional packaging changes reader responses such as trust, approach behavior, and sharing intentions.
Calls for collaboration between AI researchers and behavioural scientists to assess real-world effects on audiences.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights that optimizing for engagement or emotional resonance can have unintended consequences on information quality and public trust. It encourages evaluation frameworks that measure human response, not just model output quality.
visual_elements: Flow diagram showing AI emotional packaging → reader perception → trust/share behavior
Side-by-side comparison of neutral vs emotionally packaged news headlines
Icon set for trust, engagement, and sharing outcomes
Simple evaluation framework chart contrasting technical metrics and behavioural metrics
paper_title: Emotional optimization by newsroom AI needs behavioural evaluation
